Common questions

Do I need a referral?

No. You can book directly with any of our clinicians.

Can I get a same-day appointment?

We keep a number of appointments free every morning for urgent but non-emergency problems. Call us at 8:00.

Do you offer video consultations?

Yes, for follow-ups and many first conversations. Ask when you book.

pages.title: Appointments
pages.content:
You can book by phone, at the front desk or by sending us a message. We aim to offer every patient an appointment within the same week.

Before your visit

  • Bring a list of medicines and allergies
  • Arrive ten minutes early for a first visit
  • Let us know if you need an interpreter or step-free access

If you need to cancel, please tell us at least 24 hours ahead so we can offer the slot to someone else.

Contact the front desk

pages.title: About Us
pages.content:
Evergreen Care opened its doors in a converted bakery on Linden Avenue, with one doctor, one nurse and a waiting room that still smelled faintly of bread. Today we are a team of twelve, but the idea is the same: unhurried care from people who know your name.

Our promise

  • Appointments that start on time
  • Time to ask questions
  • Clear, written next steps

We want every visit to feel like a conversation, not a queue.

Dr. Lena Okafor

posts.title: Seven Small Habits for Better Sleep
posts.excerpt: Good sleep is less about one big change than a handful of small, boring habits repeated every evening. Here are the seven we recommend most.
posts.content:
Almost every week someone tells us they are tired all the time. Sometimes there is a medical reason we need to look into, but very often the first step is simpler: a calmer, more regular evening.

The seven habits

  1. Wake up at the same time every day, weekends included.
  2. Get daylight on your face within an hour of waking.
  3. Keep caffeine to the morning.
  4. Give your evening a slow last hour: dim lights, no work email.
  5. Keep the bedroom cool, dark and boring.
  6. If you cannot sleep after twenty minutes, get up and read somewhere else.
  7. Keep naps short and early.

Your body loves a routine. Sleep is often the first thing to improve when the day has a predictable shape.

Dr. Lena Okafor, family physician

When to talk to us

If you snore loudly, wake up gasping, or feel exhausted despite a full night in bed, please book a visit. These can be signs of conditions that are very treatable.

This article is general information to help you look after yourself. It is not a diagnosis; if you are worried about your health, please book an appointment.

comments.author: Hannah

posts.title: A Gentle Guide to Starting to Walk Again
posts.excerpt: You do not need a gym or a plan. Ten minutes after lunch is a perfectly good place to start, and here is how to build from there.
posts.content:
Walking is the most underrated thing we prescribe. It is free, gentle on the joints, good for the heart, and it tends to improve sleep and mood as a side effect.

A four-week starting plan

Go slower than you think you need to. The goal of the first month is not fitness; it is making walking a normal part of your day.

Comfortable from the start

  • Wear shoes you already find comfortable.
  • Walk with a friend or a podcast.
  • Choose a route with somewhere to sit halfway.

This article is general information to help you look after yourself. It is not a diagnosis; if you are worried about your health, please book an appointment.

posts.title: Eating Well on a Busy Week
posts.excerpt: No perfect diet required: a few reliable meals, a well-stocked cupboard and a plan for the evenings when cooking feels impossible.
posts.content:
Most of us know roughly what a balanced plate looks like. The hard part is Wednesday at seven in the evening, when everyone is hungry and nobody has a plan.

Keep in the cupboard

  • Tinned beans and lentils
  • Wholegrain pasta and rice
  • Tinned tomatoes
  • Frozen vegetables
  • Oats

Three fallback meals

  • Bean and vegetable soup
  • Eggs, greens and toast
  • Lentil pasta with tomatoes

Cook once, eat twice: double the recipe on Sunday and the busiest evening of the week is already solved.

A good diet is mostly a good shopping list.

If you are managing diabetes, kidney disease or food allergies, our practice nurse can help you adapt these ideas.

This article is general information to help you look after yourself. It is not a diagnosis; if you are worried about your health, please book an appointment.

posts.title: What to Expect at Your Annual Check-up
posts.excerpt: From blood pressure to the questions we ask about sleep and mood, here is what happens at a yearly check-up and how to prepare.
posts.content:
An annual check-up is the one appointment where nothing is wrong, and that is exactly why it is useful. It gives us a baseline and gives you time to ask the questions that never fit into a rushed visit.

Before your visit

  • Bring a list of your medicines, including vitamins.
  • Write down any questions in advance.
  • If we have asked for a blood test, book it a week before.

During the visit

We will check your blood pressure, weight and any routine screening that is due for your age. We will also ask about sleep, mood, movement and alcohol, without judgement.

Most check-ups take around thirty minutes. You will leave with a short written summary.

posts.title: Looking After Your Mind in Winter
posts.excerpt: Shorter days affect many of us. Simple ways to protect your mood through the darker months, and when to ask for more help.
posts.content:
When the days get shorter, many people notice lower energy, more sleep and less interest in things they usually enjoy. For some, it is a passing dip; for others, it is more.

Small things that help

  • A daily walk in daylight, ideally in the morning.
  • Plans with other people, even small ones.
  • A regular bedtime and wake time.
  • Moving your body most days.

Asking for help early is a sign of good self-care, not weakness.

If low mood lasts more than two weeks or affects your daily life, please talk to us. There are many good options, and you do not need to wait until things feel serious.

This article is general information to help you look after yourself. It is not a diagnosis; if you are worried about your health, please book an appointment.

comments.author: Tomas
comments.content: Gentle and practical. Sharing this with my dad.

posts.title: Keeping Children Well Through School Season
posts.excerpt: Sleep, snacks, hand-washing and the paperwork nobody remembers: a practical checklist for families at the start of the school year.
posts.content:
The first weeks of school bring new routines, new friends and, almost inevitably, new colds. Most of these pass on their own, but a little preparation helps.

Back-to-school checklist

  • Check that routine vaccinations are up to date.
  • Book an eye test if your child squints at screens or the board.
  • Agree on a school-night bedtime before term starts.
  • Pack a water bottle every day.

When to keep them at home

A high temperature, vomiting, or a child who is simply too unwell to take part should stay home. If you are unsure, call our nurse line for advice.

This article is general information to help you look after yourself. It is not a diagnosis; if you are worried about your health, please book an appointment.

posts.title: Hydration: Myths and Facts
posts.excerpt: Do you really need eight glasses a day? Does coffee count? A short, calm look at what we actually know about drinking enough.
posts.content:
Few health topics attract as many confident rules as water. Most healthy adults can simply drink when thirsty, a little more in hot weather or when exercising.

Myth

Everyone needs exactly eight glasses a day.

Fact

Needs vary with size, weather and activity. Pale yellow urine is a good everyday guide.

Myth

Coffee and tea do not count.

Fact

They do count towards your daily fluids for most people.

Older adults can feel less thirsty, so a glass with each meal is a sensible habit. If you have heart or kidney conditions, follow the advice your clinician gave you.
